niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why You See It Everywhere Now
ideas.angle: The video explains the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon where your brain, after learning a new word or seeing a specific car, starts 'filtering' it into your conscious awareness, making it look like a global coincidence.
ideas.reason: Relatable 'glitch in the matrix' experiences drive high engagement and comments. Users often experience this and think it's fate; explaining the science behind it satisfies curiosity instantly.

ideas.title: Why Beauty Blinds Your Judgment
ideas.angle: It reveals the Halo Effect: a cognitive bias where we automatically attribute positive traits like intelligence or kindness to attractive people without any evidence.
ideas.reason: Social dynamics and 'pretty privilege' are currently trending topics on TikTok and Reels. It challenges the viewer's own fairness, making it highly shareable.
sources: Edward Thorndike (1920) 'The Constant Error in Psychological Ratings'

ideas.title: Why You Overvalue Your Own Work
ideas.angle: The video shows that we value products we helped create—even if they are flawed—much more than identical items built by experts, known as the IKEA Effect.

hook.fr: Tu surestimes ce que tu crées.

ideas.reason: Explaining why we keep 'junk' or feel proud of minor DIY tasks is a universal 'lightbulb' moment. It appeals to both the DIY community and business-minded viewers.
sources: Norton, Mochon, & Ariely (2012) 'The IKEA Effect: When Labor Leads to Love'
